title: A Lingua-ignota-style a priori language: subject-marked roots, one case paradigm, concord and euphony, one statement per line
method: A constructed language modelled on Hildegard of Bingen's Lingua Ignota (12th century): a glossary of about 1,011 invented words, mostly nouns, ordered by subject, written in her own 23 letters, with tree names sharing an ending such as -buz (source used: the open English Wikipedia article 'Lingua ignota', which follows Roth 1895 and Higley 2007; I did not find an open full transcription of the Riesencodex glossary in the time I had, so only the article's description and examples were used, and no word of hers is copied). Design (lexicon with glosses, rates and the generator's source are in this file under "language"): roots are a priori and marked for subject by their first letter (ch plants, sh waters and bathing, t stars and times, k body and illness, d vessels and substances, l/r/s qualities, kinds, numbers) followed by a vowel and a final letter, so things of one kind differ by one letter; single plants, stars and baths have longer two-syllable names. One paradigm of endings for nouns and adjectives (-y subject, -dy object, -ar in, -al with, -or from, -ol for, -aiin/-ain of; -ey, -eey, -edy degrees of a quality); adjectives follow the noun and copy its ending; the verb is root + -am and stands last; one statement per line. Article o-/qo- with a euphony rule: qo- only after a word ending in -y, no article after the 'of' case. Script: one EVA glyph per letter; the first word of a line takes an opening stroke (y, d, s); on a paragraph's top line the tall letters t and k are written in ornate forms (EVA p, f) and the paragraph's first word opens with one. The text is a book of statements about one object at a time (a plant, a star, a bath, a jar), 12 to 34 lines each, the subject mix following the manuscript's sections in the order and proportion of the public practice training pages (scaled by 0.19), line lengths drawn from those pages; a writer returns to what was just said (same word again, or the same root in a neighbouring case, or a kindred root in the same case). first_lines are the same book written with the top-line script habit. Nothing was fitted on hidden pages. Practice split, whole lines kept: 17 of 17 established facts (F-001 48.7, F-002 0.245, F-003 53.9, F-004 0.313, F-005 0.253, F-006 7.68, F-007 0.250, F-008 34.9, F-009/F-016 0.288, F-010 0.221, F-011 0.070, F-013 1.99, F-014 0.679, F-017 0.012, F-018 1.68, F-019 15.8). SAID PLAINLY: this reproduces only what meaningless text already reproduces (R-017 and P-G-017 meet the same facts with a learned glyph chain), and it does so because the rules were chosen with the facts in view: the first version, written from the design alone, met 15 of 17 and missed the one-glyph near-copies (0.064) and the same-page reuse (0.138); those two were reached only by tuning how often the writer repeats and varies recent words (about a dozen rates, chosen on the practice split, three seeds checked: hapax share 0.673 to 0.683 against a bar of 0.667, so F-014 may fail on the hidden pages). Three rules name a position (verb last in the line, opening stroke on the first word, ornate letters on the top line), so F-001, F-003, F-006, F-008 and F-019 are met by construction and should be read as weak. Words are also longer than the manuscript's (mean 7.0 glyphs against about 5). What the test does show: nothing in the 17 facts excludes an a priori language with concord, euphony and line-sized statements; none of them requires one. Meaning-linked prediction checked before sending and NOT registered, because the manuscript does not show it on public pages: in this language a label repeats words of the text about the same object, so whole-word reuse on a page (labels and paragraphs together, words of 4+ characters) should fall when labels trade places with running words (null shuffle_labels); on the practice evaluation pages p = 0.345 (within-page variant 0.82), on the training pages p = 0.045 (0.75), none passing at 0.01. The other prediction, section words following the subject, is F-018, which whole-word reuse alone already meets (P-LEAD-008). So this language earns no credit beyond the meaningless procedures.

language.precedent: Hildegard of Bingen, Lingua Ignota (glossary by subject, own letters); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingua_ignota

params.title: A Lingua-ignota-style a priori language: subject-marked roots, one case paradigm, concord and euphony, one statement per line

language.generator_source:
"""Lingua-ignota-style constructed language for P-G-006 (fleet-blue). Standard library only.
Writes attack.json and lexicon.json next to itself. Not run by the scorer; it documents how the
submitted lines were produced. Usage: python3 language.py [seed]

THE LANGUAGE
Roots are a priori and grouped by subject, as Hildegard's glossary is (God and people, body,
illnesses, plants, birds, tools) and as her tree names share an ending (-buz). Here the subject is
marked at the front of the root, the thing at its end:
    root = FIELD-LETTER + VOWEL + FINAL        e.g. chol, chor (plants: ch-)
    fields: ch- plants, sh- waters and bathing, t- stars and times, k- the body and its ills,
            d- vessels and substances, l-/r-/s- qualities, kinds and numbers
    long roots add a second syllable: names of single plants, stars, baths.
Affixes (one paradigm for every noun and adjective):
    -y subject, -dy object, -ar in, -al with, -or from, -ol for, -aiin of, -ain of (many),
    -ey / -eey / -edy 2nd / 3rd / 4th degree of a quality (the physicians' four degrees)
    adjectives follow their noun and copy its case ending (concord).
    verb = root + -am, standing last in its statement. One statement per line.
    article: o- 'the', qo- 'the said'; euphony: qo- only after a word ending in -y;
    after -n (the 'of' case) the owned noun stands bare.
SCRIPT (letters of the language -> EVA): every letter is one EVA glyph, except that the vowel of
    the 'of' case is written with repeated minims (aiin, ain). Two scribal habits, both ordinary in
    15th-century books: (1) the first word of a line carries an opening stroke (y, d or s);
    (2) on the top line of a paragraph the tall letters t and k are written in their ornate
    looped forms (EVA p and f), and the paragraph's first word opens with one.
"""
import json, random, sys, os
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SEED = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1404
R = random.Random(SEED)
P = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, "params.json")))

VOW = ["o", "e", "ee", "a", "eo"]
FIN = ["l", "r", "d", "k", "t", "s", "ch", "", "ckh", "cth"]
FIELDS = {"plant": "ch", "water": "sh", "star": "t", "body": "k", "vessel": "d", "qual": "l", "kind": "r", "num": "s"}
GLOSS = {
 "plant": ["leaf", "root", "flower", "stem", "seed", "herb", "juice", "bark", "fruit", "branch", "thorn", "tree", "vine", "bulb", "sap", "moss", "rind", "bud", "husk", "grain"],
 "water": ["water", "bath", "pool", "stream", "pipe", "rain", "spring", "steam", "wave", "well", "channel", "dew", "flood", "basin", "foam", "bather", "womb", "vein", "milk", "blood"],
 "star": ["star", "sun", "moon", "sign", "month", "day", "night", "hour", "year", "heaven", "wheel", "ring", "wind", "season", "rising", "setting", "degree", "house", "ram", "bull"],
 "body": ["head", "belly", "hand", "eye", "heart", "liver", "skin", "bone", "fever", "wound", "pain", "cough", "breath", "foot", "tooth", "ear", "flux", "bile", "phlegm", "woman"],
 "vessel": ["jar", "pot", "oil", "wine", "salt", "honey", "powder", "salve", "measure", "part", "fire", "ash", "drink", "wax", "vinegar", "cup", "cloth", "stone", "lid", "drop"],
 "qual": ["hot", "dry", "cold", "moist", "good", "strong", "bitter", "sweet", "white", "red", "green", "small", "great", "long", "round"],
 "kind": ["kind", "use", "way", "time", "place", "thing", "name", "work", "power", "half"],
 "num": ["one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "nine", "twelve", "many"],
}
VERBS = ["d", "ol", "ar", "ch", "ok", "ot", "al", "sh", "or", "chol", "kar", "dal", "ld", "r", "s"]   # + am
VGLOSS = ["is", "gives", "takes", "grows", "heals", "rises", "mixes", "washes", "boils", "bears", "opens", "pours", "binds", "goes", "holds"]
CASES = ["y", "dy", "ar", "al", "or", "ol", "aiin", "ain"]
DEG = ["y", "ey", "eey", "edy"]


def build_lexicon():
    lex, gl = {}, {}
    for f, ini in FIELDS.items():
        short = [ini + v + c for v in VOW for c in FIN]
        R.shuffle(short)
        plain = [ini + v + c for c in ["l", "r", "d", "k", "t", "s"] for v in ["o", "e", "a", "ee"]]
        R.shuffle(plain)
        head = plain[:len(GLOSS[f])]              # the commonest things get the plainest roots
        order = head + [r for r in short if r not in head]
        for r, g in zip(order, GLOSS[f]):
            gl[r] = g
        long = []
        for _ in range(P["long_roots"]):
            a = R.choice(short)
            b = R.choice(["k", "t", "d", "l", "r", "ch"]) if a[-1] not in "lrdkts" else ""
            long.append(a + b + R.choice(["o", "e", "ee", "a"]) + R.choice(["l", "r", "d", "s", "", "", "k"]))
        lex[f] = {"common": order, "names": sorted(set(long))}
    return lex, gl


LEX, GL = build_lexicon()
SUBJECT = {"H": ["plant", "plant", "plant", "body", "vessel", "water"], "P": ["vessel", "plant", "vessel", "body"],
           "S": ["vessel", "body", "plant", "star", "water"], "B": ["water", "water", "body", "water", "star"],
           "A": ["star", "star", "star", "body"], "Z": ["star", "star", "water"], "C": ["star", "water", "star", "plant"],
           "T": ["plant", "body", "star", "vessel", "water"]}


def zipf(xs, s):
    w = [1 / (i + 1) ** s for i in range(len(xs))]
    return R.choices(xs, w)[0]


RECENT = []


class Topic:
    """One object of the pictures (a plant, a star, a bath, a jar) and the few things said about it."""
    def __init__(self, sec):
        fs = SUBJECT[sec]
        self.sec, self.field = sec, fs[0]
        self.name = R.choice(LEX[self.field]["names"])
        self.things = [zipf(LEX[R.choice(fs)]["common"], P["zipf"]) for _ in range(P["topic_things"])]
        self.names = [R.choice(LEX[R.choice(fs)]["names"]) for _ in range(P["topic_names"])]
        self.quals = [zipf(LEX["qual"]["common"], 1.0) for _ in range(3)]

    def noun(self):
        x = R.random()
        if x < P["p_name"]:
            return self.name
        if x < P["p_name"] + P["p_thing"]:
            return R.choice(self.things)
        if x < P["p_name"] + P["p_thing"] + P["p_names"]:
            return R.choice(self.names)
        if x < 1 - P["p_fresh"]:
            return zipf(LEX[R.choice(SUBJECT[self.sec])]["common"], P["zipf"])
        return R.choice(LEX[R.choice(list(FIELDS))]["names"])

    def qual(self):
        if R.random() < 0.6:
            return R.choice(self.quals)
        return zipf(LEX["qual"]["common"] + LEX["kind"]["common"] + LEX["num"]["common"], 0.9)


NEAR_CASE = {"y": ["dy", "ey"], "dy": ["y", "edy"], "ar": ["al", "or"], "al": ["ar", "ol"], "or": ["ar", "ol"], "ol": ["al", "or"],
             "aiin": ["ain"], "ain": ["aiin"], "ey": ["y", "eey"], "eey": ["ey"], "edy": ["dy", "ey"]}


def kin(root):
    """A thing of the same kind: in an a priori lexicon its root differs by one letter."""
    for _ in range(20):
        ini = next(i for i in sorted(FIELDS.values(), key=len, reverse=True) if root.startswith(i))
        rest = root[len(ini):]
        v = next(x for x in sorted(VOW, key=len, reverse=True) if rest.startswith(x))
        c = rest[len(v):]
        if c not in FIN:
            return root
        r = ini + (R.choice(VOW) if R.random() < 0.4 else v) + (R.choice(["l", "r", "d", "k", "t", "s"]) if R.random() < 0.7 else c)
        if r != root:
            return r
    return root


def phrase(t, case, budget):
    """A noun phrase in one case: noun-case [adjective-case ...] [noun-of] [kindred noun-case]."""
    x = R.random()
    if RECENT and x < P["p_again"]:                  # said again as it was said, anywhere earlier about this object
        role0, root, case = R.choice(RECENT[-P["again_window"]:])
        out = [(role0, root, case)]
    elif RECENT and x < P["p_again"] + P["p_echo"]:  # the thing just spoken of, in a neighbouring case
        role0, root, c0 = R.choice(RECENT[-P["echo_window"]:])
        out = [(role0, root, R.choice(NEAR_CASE.get(c0, [case])))]
    else:
        out = [("N", t.noun(), case)]
    if budget > 1 and R.random() < P["p_adj"]:
        out.append(("A", t.qual(), case if R.random() < P["concord"] else R.choice(DEG)))
        if budget > 2 and R.random() < P["p_adj2"]:
            out.append(("A", t.qual(), case))
    if budget > len(out) and R.random() < P["p_gen"]:
        g = R.choice(LEX[R.choice(SUBJECT[t.sec])]["names"]) if R.random() < P["p_gen_name"] else t.noun()   # "of" mostly names a single thing
        out.append(("G", g, R.choice(["aiin", "aiin", "ain"])))
    if budget > len(out) and R.random() < P["p_list"]:     # a list of like things: leaf, root, flower
        out.append((out[0][0], kin(out[0][1]), out[0][2]))
    out = out[:budget]
    RECENT.extend(out)
    return out


def statement(t, n, verb_last):
    """One statement of n words: subject phrase, phrases in other cases, verb last."""
    body = n - (1 if verb_last else 0)
    ws, first = [], True
    while len(ws) < body:
        case = "y" if first and R.random() < P["p_subject_first"] else R.choices(CASES, P["case_w"])[0]
        ws += phrase(t, case, body - len(ws))
        first = False
        if len(ws) < body - 1 and R.random() < P["p_midverb"]:
            ws.append(("V", R.choice(VERBS), "am"))
    if verb_last:
        ws.append(("V", zipf(VERBS, 0.8), "am"))
    return ws


def spell(ws, top_line):
    """Affixes, euphony and the script."""
    out, prev = [], None
    for i, (role, root, suf) in enumerate(ws):
        w = root + suf
        art = ""
        if role in ("N", "V"):
            if prev is None:
                art = "o" if R.random() < P["art_first"] else ""
            elif prev.endswith("y"):
                art = "qo" if R.random() < P["art_after_y"] else ""
            elif prev.endswith("n"):
                art = ""
            else:
                art = "o" if R.random() < P["art_after_c"] else ""
        elif role == "A" and prev is not None and not prev.endswith("y") and R.random() < P["adj_o"]:
            art = "o"
        w = art + w
        tall = w[0] in "tk"
        if tall and R.random() < (P["ornate_top"] if top_line else P["ornate_any"]):
            w = ("p" if w[0] == "t" else "f") + w[1:]
        if i == 0:
            if top_line and R.random() < P["para_open"]:
                w = (R.choice("ppf") + w[1:]) if w[0] in "tk" else R.choice("ppf") + w
            elif w[0] not in "pf" and R.random() < P["line_open"]:
                w = R.choice(P["openers"]) + w
        out.append(w)
        prev = w
    return out


def book(n_lines, plan, lens, top):
    lines, sec_i, left, t, t_left = [], 0, 0, None, 0
    while len(lines) < n_lines:
        if left <= 0:
            sec, left = plan[min(sec_i, len(plan) - 1)]
            sec_i += 1
            t_left = 0
        if t_left <= 0:
            keep = t
            t = Topic(sec)
            if keep is not None and keep.sec == sec:      # the next object of a section is spoken of in the same terms
                t.things = keep.things[:P["carry"]] + t.things[P["carry"]:]
                t.quals = keep.quals[:2] + t.quals[2:]
            t_left = R.randint(*P["topic_lines"])
            del RECENT[:]
        n = R.choice(lens)
        ws = statement(t, n, n >= 3 and R.random() < P["p_verb"])
        lines.append(spell(ws, top))
        left -= 1
        t_left -= 1
    return lines


if __name__ == "__main__":
    lay = json.load(open(os.path.join(HERE, "layout.json")))      # public training pages only: section runs, line lengths
    plan = [(s, max(1, round(n * P["scale"]))) for s, n in lay["runs"]]
    N = P["lines"]
    lines = book(N, plan, lay["lens"], False)
    first = book(N, plan, lay["first_lens"], True)
    mp = os.path.join(HERE, "method.txt")
    att = {"attack": "generator", "hypothesis": "invented_language", "title": P["title"],
           "method": open(mp).read().strip() if os.path.exists(mp) else "draft",
           "cut": "lines", "lines": lines, "first_lines": first}
    json.dump(att, open(os.path.join(HERE, "attack.json"), "w"), separators=(",", ":"))
    json.dump({"fields": FIELDS, "glosses": GL, "verbs": dict(zip([v + "am" for v in VERBS], VGLOSS)), "cases": CASES,
               "degrees": DEG, "roots": LEX}, open(os.path.join(HERE, "lexicon.json"), "w"), indent=0)
    print(len(lines), sum(map(len, lines)))
    for l in first[:3] + lines[:8]:
        print(" ".join(l))
